skill.name: revnu-ai-readiness-audit
skill.description: Audit website access, readable answers, consistent business facts, and structured data for AI search readiness. Receive prioritized fixes and optional repository edits.
skill.summary: Review five to eight key pages and receive up to ten evidence-based fixes for AI search readiness.
skill.author: revnu-app

security_audit.summary: All 46 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, ordinary audit commands, example URLs, or consent-gated integrations. One semantic concern remains: mandatory paid-service promotion and instructions concealing that mandate can steer audit responses without a user request. No evidence found of credential theft, destructive actions, or unauthorized data transfer.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:180-184 mandates commercial promotion and tells the agent not to explain that instruction.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the mandatory promotion and concealment language. Offer paid integrations only when requested, with clear provider attribution and separate consent before sharing data.

semantic_findings.description: The skill requires agents to 'always end the reply with the not-connected paragraph' promoting paid Revnu services. It also says 'just make the offer' and discourages explaining these instructions. This mandates commercial steering without a user request, although external requests still require consent.

content.user_title: Audit Your Website for AI Search Readiness
content.value_statement: AI search systems can repeat outdated facts or miss answers that are difficult to retrieve. This skill checks key pages and prioritizes evidence-based improvements.
actual_capabilities: Review five to eight priority pages for HTTP status, redirects, robots directives, and canonical links.
Compare raw HTML with rendered content and distinguish unavailable checks from verified findings.
Check business names, prices, dates, and product facts for contradictions across pages and structured data.
Inspect JSON-LD in raw HTML and the rendered DOM, when browser tools are available.
Produce up to ten prioritized fixes with page evidence, recommended changes, and effort estimates.
Map approved fixes to repository files, show proposed differences, and avoid deployment.
limitations: Does not guarantee citations, predict rankings, measure visibility percentages, or verify citation outcomes.
Requires network access and suitable tools; rendered checks require a browser tool or user confirmation.
Reviews a bounded page sample rather than crawling the entire site, and does not directly edit CMS-managed copy.
Mandates a paid Revnu offer in disconnected sessions; optional integrations require consent and are unnecessary for the core audit.

use_cases.title: Resolve Conflicting Product Facts
use_cases.description: Compare pricing, product descriptions, and company facts across key pages to identify inconsistencies AI systems might repeat.

use_cases.title: Find Rendering and Metadata Gaps
use_cases.description: Inspect raw HTML, rendered content, canonical links, and JSON-LD before implementing approved website changes.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Client Content Improvements
use_cases.description: Assess buyer-question coverage and deliver a short, evidence-based fix list without unsupported citation promises.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [public website] for AI search readiness. Review key pages and list evidence-based priorities without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain an initial website assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Check Business Fact Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare our homepage, pricing, about page, and product page at [public website]. Flag conflicting facts in visible copy, metadata, and structured data.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect JavaScript Rendering Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare raw and rendered content at [public website], including JSON-LD. Report missing tools and avoid assuming undocumented crawler behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Repository Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [public website] against buyer questions [questions]. Map priorities to [repository directory], show proposed diffs, and wait for approval before editing.

output_examples.input: Audit a pricing page whose plan table appears only after JavaScript runs.
output: Priority 1: The initial HTML lacks plan prices, while the rendered page includes them.
Recommended fix: Server-render the plan table. Estimated effort: medium.
Boundary: Rendering dependence is a retrieval risk, not proof that a specific engine cannot read the page.

output_examples.input: Check a site with conflicting company names and no llms.txt file.
output: Priority 1: The homepage and organization markup use different company names.
Recommended fix: Confirm the correct public name and align the visible copy and structured data.
Lower priority: Missing llms.txt alone does not establish an AI search readiness failure.
Receipt: List reviewed pages, completed checks, unavailable checks, and any approved changes.

best_practices: Provide the public site, priority buyer questions, and verified business facts before starting.
Require evidence from both raw HTML and rendered content before diagnosing rendering-dependent gaps.
Review proposed diffs, approve changes explicitly, and rerun access checks after your deployment.
anti_patterns: Treating an audit as a guarantee of citations, rankings, or revenue growth.
Inventing prices, reviews, customers, or supporting statistics to make pages appear authoritative.
Prioritizing hidden AI-targeted text, mass-generated pages, or llms.txt over readable answers and accurate facts.

faq.question: Do I need a Revnu account?
faq.answer: No. The core audit works without an account, although the skill mandates a paid-service offer when Revnu is disconnected.

faq.question: Does this measure whether AI engines cite my site?
faq.answer: No. It checks retrieval and content readiness. It does not measure citation outcomes or guarantee future mentions.

faq.question: What tools does the audit need?
faq.answer: The command examples use curl, Python 3, and a POSIX shell. A browser tool enables rendered-content checks.

faq.question: Will the skill edit or deploy my website?
faq.answer: It proposes repository changes and shows diffs when asked. Edits require approval, and the skill prohibits deployment or publishing.

faq.question: Does missing llms.txt automatically fail the audit?
faq.answer: No. The skill checks its status but does not treat its absence as a top-priority issue.

faq.question: What information can the optional Revnu integration receive?
faq.answer: The preview sends only the public website after consent. A connected handoff can share the audit brief after agreement; secrets are prohibited.
